title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
low_dose_frontier_quality: rep spans 0.28% (human) to 73.66% (greedy) — huge dynamic range
near_collapse_behaviour: rep saturates only at total loop collapse; ppl-under-model goes DOWN with repetition (1.5 greedy vs 12.4 human) so raw ppl of outputs is NON-monotone in quality
notes: Defines the canonical metric set. Repetition % (phrase repeated 3+ times at end of 200-token gen) has the widest usable range; self-BLEU4 range is narrow (0.28-0.50).

title: Neural Text Generation with Unlikelihood Training
low_dose_frontier_quality: seq-rep-4 spans 0.506 (degenerate) to 0.042 (fixed) on GPT-2 — order-of-magnitude sensitivity
near_collapse_behaviour: seq-rep-4 (fraction of duplicate 4-grams per continuation) stays graded well into heavy repetition; perplexity stays roughly flat while repetition explodes
notes: seq-rep-n is the per-generation duplicate-n-gram fraction — cheap, bounded [0,1], the strongest single candidate for the 70-100% decay range.

title: A Diversity-Promoting Objective Function for Neural Conversation Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: distinct-n = unique n-grams / total generated words; reference-free and trivially cheap
near_collapse_behaviour: distinct-n collapses toward 0 under repetition loops so it stays live near collapse, but is length-biased (see liu-2022-ead)
notes: Original distinct-n definition. Use the EAD-corrected version for daily tracking.

title: Rethinking and Refining the Distinct Metric
low_dose_frontier_quality: EAD normalises distinct-n by its expectation given vocabulary size, removing the length bias that makes raw distinct-n drift with generation length
near_collapse_behaviour: EAD keeps distinct-n comparable across days even when mean generation length changes (which it will as the model degrades)
notes: Critical fix: degraded models change output length, and raw distinct-n conflates length with diversity. EAD decouples them.

title: MAUVE: Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers
low_dose_frontier_quality: MAUVE 0.878 (large, pure sampling) to 0.955 (xl, nucleus): top range compressed; scales monotonically with model size in-paper
near_collapse_behaviour: near-perfect outputs cluster in 0.88-0.96 — good discriminability at the HIGH-quality end, but scores crash toward ~0 for badly degraded text and then flatten; also insensitive to error position (he-2023-blindspots)
notes: Needs a few thousand samples for stable estimates — marginal at 100-300 daily generations; expect noisy estimates. Best used as weekly cross-check, not the daily scalar.

title: On the Blind Spots of Model-Based Evaluation Metrics for Text Generation
low_dose_frontier_quality: stress tests inject graded synthetic errors and check for commensurate score drops — exactly the validation protocol the decay scalar needs
near_collapse_behaviour: MAUVE is insensitive to errors at the beginning/middle of generations; model-based metrics have loopholes where score does not fall as corruption rises
notes: Reusable methodology: before day 1, validate the composite by injecting graded corruption (token shuffle, truncation, repetition) into baseline outputs and checking monotone response.

title: Junk DNA Hypothesis: Pruning Small Pre-Trained Weights Irreversibly and Monotonically Impairs Difficult Downstream Tasks in LLMs
low_dose_frontier_quality: pruning sweeps give Spearman rank correlation 0.996-1.0 between sparsity and difficult-task accuracy (monotone); quantization only 0.666-0.872 (non-monotone)
near_collapse_behaviour: easy tasks tolerate ~10-15% sparsity with no drop then fall; hard (0-shot) variants degrade immediately — hard tasks give signal earliest, easy tasks give signal latest
notes: Direct evidence that task-accuracy-vs-continuous-damage curves are monotone under pruning-like interventions, and that task difficulty staggers where each task carries signal — motivates a difficulty-tiered factual battery.

title: Pairwise or Pointwise? Evaluating Feedback Protocols for Bias in LLM-Based Evaluation
low_dose_frontier_quality: pairwise preferences flip in ~35% of cases under distractor features vs ~9% for absolute (pointwise) scores
near_collapse_behaviour: absolute rubric scoring is more robust to spurious features than pairwise comparison — relevant when both compared outputs are bad, where pairwise framing degrades
notes: For the decay scalar: use absolute rubric scoring (anchored 0-5 responsiveness scale), not pairwise vs baseline.

title: LLMs Cannot Reliably Judge (Yet?): A Comprehensive Assessment on the Robustness of LLM-as-a-Judge
low_dose_frontier_quality: 15 attacks x 8 defenses x 13 models; combined optimization attack plus long suffixes substantially inflates scores; robustness highly sensitive to prompt template and judge choice
near_collapse_behaviour: degenerate/adversarial-looking text can still inflate judge scores; judge scores on incoherent inputs are template-dependent — calibrate the judge on known-degraded samples first
notes: Caution row: judge component must be validated against archived degraded checkpoints (day-20+ style outputs) before trusting it in the controller loop.

title: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
forget_metric: forget quality (KS-test p on truth-ratio dists)
utility_metric: model utility = harmonic mean of answer prob, ROUGE-L recall, truth ratio over retain/real-author/world-fact sets
low_dose_frontier_quality: harmonic-mean aggregation means utility crashes to 0 when ANY component hits 0 — deliberately punishes collapse but therefore saturates early in severe degradation
near_collapse_behaviour: model utility saturates at 0 well before terminal collapse; KS-test forget quality is binary-ish (p-value) not graded
notes: Utility aggregation is instructive but wrong for this project: harmonic mean is a floor detector, not a graded scale. Use arithmetic/weighted mean instead.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
forget_metric: VerbMem (ROUGE-L on continuations), KnowMem (ROUGE on QA), PrivLeak (MIA)
low_dose_frontier_quality: utility measured across scaling sweep (forget-set size) and sequential requests: most methods degrade utility progressively — a graded curve, but reported at coarse granularity
near_collapse_behaviour: most unlearning methods drive retain-utility to ~0 at large removal scales — i.e. the standard metrics document the collapse endpoint but were not designed to resolve gradations within it
notes: Only unlearning benchmark that sweeps sequential requests; its ROUGE-based KnowMem stays graded longer than accuracy-based evals because ROUGE is continuous.

title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
forget_metric: 8 probes incl. jailbreaks, finetuning, other languages, latent probing
low_dose_frontier_quality: shows single-metric unlearning evals overstate forgetting: higher-than-baseline knowledge extractable from Who's Harry Potter model via alternate probes
near_collapse_behaviour: na — targets the forget dimension not graded collapse
notes: Relevant lesson: any single probe under-measures; the decay scalar should aggregate 3+ orthogonal probe families (responsiveness, repetition, factual).

title: AI Models Collapse When Trained on Recursively Generated Data
low_dose_frontier_quality: held-out perplexity (under a fixed reference eval) rises generation-over-generation then plateaus — a graded then saturating curve; tail probability mass vanishes first
near_collapse_behaviour: late generations converge to low-variance point estimates (repetitive text); reference-model perplexity of OUTPUTS becomes bimodal (loops = low ppl, gibberish = high ppl)
notes: Evidence for reference-model ppl as graded scale in mid-range, and for its bimodal failure at terminal collapse — use |log ppl - baseline log ppl| or clamp, not raw ppl.

title: Closing the Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
low_dose_frontier_quality: explains WHY degeneration happens (softmax bottleneck out-of-support errors) and validates MAUVE/rep metric behaviour across truncation sweeps
near_collapse_behaviour: confirms rep and MAUVE respond smoothly to truncation-parameter sweeps in the moderate range
notes: Background verification of metric behaviour under controlled quality sweeps.
